newsitem.title: USA: Exxon says cash flow strong.
newsitem.headline: Exxon says cash flow strong.

text.p: Exxon Corp Chairman Lee Raymond on Wednesday said the company, coming off a year of record earnings, continues to make progress this year with strong cash flow.

"Our cash flow has remained strong, enabling us to fund a growing capital program, improve our financial position and continue to increase annual dividend payments," Raymond said at the company's shareholder meeting.
Raymond also said the company will step up its stock repurchase program, but he did not set a target for the buyback.
The company raised its dividend earlier to $0.41 a share from $0.395 a share as adjusted for a two-for-one stock split that was effective last month.

Since 1983, Exxon has repurchased 550 million treasury shares for $18.8 billion, representing 32 percent of the stock outstanding at the start of 1983. The company now has 1.242 billion shares outstanding on a pre-split basis.

The shareholder meeting was enlivened by strong criticism of the company's executive compensation program, with some shareholders calling the compensation "obscene" and likening executives to "robber barons" of the past.

Raymond's total compensation including salary and stock options according to the speakers approached about $11 million in the past three years. He made about $4 million last year, according to the company's proxy.
But a shareholder proposal to require more detailed reporting on executive pay was soundly defeated.
Raymond defended the program, saying it was needed to retain the best management at the multi-national company and stock options were required to align employees to the company.
"I don't set my pay," Raymond told reporters, noting that his compensation was set by an outside committee of directors.
